name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,809

entries.clue: Crop brassica from frames (4)

indicatorNotes.frames: the phrase frames, or encloses, the answer

annotation.surface: A gardener lifting cabbages out of cold frames.
annotation.walkthrough: In the vegetable-plot picture 'Crop' is a harvest; here it is a haircut, and 'frames' is doing the enclosing.
annotation.definitionFit: A crop is a short haircut, and an Afro is a hairstyle.

entries.clue: 'Womaniser with band!' It's what they called Mozart (8)

blocks.note: a wolf is a man who chases women
a gang is a band of people

annotation.surface: A gossipy remark that the composer Mozart had a reputation as a ladies' man with a band.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Mozart's famously racy reputation; the definition is a whole phrase pointing to his first name.
annotation.definitionFit: Mozart's first name was Wolfgang.

entries.clue: Pine tar soap finally running out (4)

indicatorNotes.running out: that letter runs out of PITCH, leaving it

blocks.note: last letter of soaP, removed from PITCH

annotation.surface: A bathroom shelf where the pine-tar soap is nearly used up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pine tar soap' reads as one product; 'Pine' is split off as a verb meaning long for.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for longing: an itch to travel is a restless yearning, the sense 'pine' has as a verb.

entries.clue: Bound to be penny amongst swept up leaves (8)

indicatorNotes.amongst: P goes amongst the letters of the reversed word
indicatorNotes.swept up: in a down answer, 'up' turns the word round

blocks.note: leaves = departs, as a train leaves; read upwards in a down entry
p = penny, the abbreviation on British coins, slipped in among the reversed letters

annotation.surface: Someone sweeping up autumn leaves and finding a penny among them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb departs; 'swept up' makes it read backwards in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Tied down with straps, the literal sense of bound; the surface's 'bound to be' hides it as a phrase meaning certain.

entries.clue: Fighting in Metro regularly upset underground network (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take every other letter of 'in Metro'
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down answer, upset turns the letters upside down, i.e. reverses them

blocks.note: the even letters of iN mEtRo are NER, reversed to REN

annotation.surface: A fight breaking out on the Metro, the underground train network.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at a city's underground railway; the answer is the tunnels rabbits dig.
annotation.definitionFit: A warren is a network of rabbit burrows below ground.

entries.clue: Foreign expat nobly yielding section of field (7,3)

indicatorNotes.Foreign: foreign means strange, so the letters come out altered

annotation.surface: An expatriate abroad graciously giving up a patch of farmland.
annotation.walkthrough: The field sounds agricultural; it is a football pitch, where the penalty box is the marked area in front of goal.
annotation.definitionFit: On a football pitch this is the marked rectangle in front of each goal, one section of the field of play.

entries.clue: Drunk husband drinking more getting half-cut in plane (6)

indicatorNotes.drinking: SOT H takes MO inside, as a drinker takes in drink
indicatorNotes.half-cut: MORE cut in half leaves MO

blocks.note: first half of MORE, placed inside SOT: S(MO)OT

annotation.surface: A drunken husband getting more and more tipsy on a flight.
annotation.walkthrough: The plane is not an aircraft but the carpenter's verb; 'half-cut', British slang for drunk, is really an instruction to halve MORE.
annotation.definitionFit: A carpenter's plane shaves wood flat, so as a verb plane is a plain synonym for making even.

entries.clue: Princess forbidden to go out of bounds (4)

indicatorNotes.to go out of bounds: the bounds, the first and last letters, go out

blocks.note: forbidden = banned; its bounds are the first and last letters
the outer letters B and D, which go

annotation.surface: A royal being told certain areas are off-limits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' seems to go with 'forbidden' as a no-entry sign; it is the instruction to strip BANNED's outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Anne is the Princess Royal, daughter of Queen Elizabeth II.

entries.clue: Cafe's penultimate potato dish; one's left in reserve (5)

indicatorNotes.penultimate: penultimate means last but one, so take the last-but-one letter of 'Cafe'
indicatorNotes.left: left as in departed: the I has left ROSTI and is gone

blocks.note: rösti is a Swiss fried potato cake
one = I, removed from ROSTI to leave ROST

annotation.surface: A cafe menu where the last-but-one potato dish has one portion held back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In reserve' looks like the stock of dishes; 'reserve' alone is the definition, meaning coolness of manner.
annotation.definitionFit: Frost is a chilly reserve in someone's manner.

entries.clue: Cabinetmakers, perhaps, or carpenters smartened up? (9)

indicatorNotes.up: smartened is stirred up into a new order

annotation.surface: Woodworkers who have tidied themselves up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smartened up' reads as one phrasal verb; split it, and 'up' stirs the letters of SMARTENED.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: cabinetmakers and carpenters are both skilled manual workers who follow a trade.

entries.clue: Article penned by sour character not being broadcast (3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.penned by: THE is shut inside OFF AIR like an animal in a pen

blocks.note: an air is a manner or character

annotation.surface: A newspaper article written by a sour personality that never gets published.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing the article; it means enclosed. 'Sour character' looks like one grumpy person but is two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom from radio and television: a programme off the air is not currently being transmitted.

entries.clue: All-rounder oddly only making single (5)

annotation.surface: A cricket all-rounder who managed only a single run.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket an all-rounder bats and bowls, and a single is one run; here 'single' means unaccompanied.
annotation.definitionFit: Single, as in on one's own, means alone.

entries.clue: Son snubbed fish, going back for other seafood (7)

indicatorNotes.snubbed: snubbed puns on snub, short: POLLACK is cut short
indicatorNotes.going back: the shortened fish is read backwards

blocks.note: pollack is a sea fish; drop the K, then reverse POLLAC to CALLOP

annotation.surface: A son rejecting the fish on his plate and ordering some other seafood instead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' reads as rejected; here it means docked, as in a snub nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A scallop is a shellfish, a seafood other than the fish already used.

entries.clue: Goals for goalies but not for strikers? (5)

annotation.definition: Goals for goalies but not for strikers?

blocks.note: read as the football scores a goalkeeper concedes, and meant as the aims a goalkeeper has
a striker wants the ball in the net, so every stop by the keeper thwarts them

annotation.surface: A football pundit's quip about what each player wants.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goals' here means aims: a goalkeeper aims to make saves, which a striker never wants to see.
annotation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper's stops are what they aim for, and each one denies a striker, so both halves of the clue point at the same act.

entries.clue: Cheese from a can spread with relish (10)

indicatorNotes.spread: the letters are spread about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, joined 'with' the first part

annotation.surface: Tinned cheese spread smeared on with pickle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spread' and 'relish' feel like sandwich fillings; one stirs the letters and the other is fodder. Lancashire is an English county that names a crumbly cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this crumbly white cheese takes its name from the county in north-west England where it is made.

entries.clue: Nicked, distinguished companion is put inside (7)

indicatorNotes.is put inside: British slang for jailed, used literally: CH is put inside NOTED

blocks.note: CH = Companion of Honour, a British order

annotation.surface: A notable's companion arrested and jailed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' and 'put inside' are British slang for arrested and jailed; here nicked means cut with a small notch.
annotation.definitionFit: Nicked in the sense of cut with a small V-shaped mark; the surface pushes the slang sense of arrested.

entries.clue: Act after act succeeded ... they're all dead now (5)

blocks.note: a second DO follows the first
s = succeeded, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A long variety show running act after act until the audience has expired.
annotation.walkthrough: The dodo is the proverbial extinct bird, hence 'all dead now'.
annotation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius is the byword for extinction, as in 'dead as a dodo', so 'all dead now' fits.

entries.clue: A choosy eater, teenage visitor returned sandwiches (5)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the words sandwich the answer between them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of teenage and the start of visitor, then read backwards

annotation.surface: A fussy teenage guest sending back the sandwiches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like the food sent back; it is the verb, holding the answer inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A vegan chooses carefully what to eat, avoiding all animal products.

entries.clue: Shorten short dwarf (3)

indicatorNotes.short: DOCK falls short of its last letter

blocks.note: to dock is to shorten; remove the final K

annotation.surface: Cutting a small person down to size.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like part of the definition beside 'dwarf'; it is the instruction to cut DOCK.
annotation.definitionFit: Doc is one of the Seven Dwarfs in Snow White.

entries.clue: Top performers at most AGMs - the Chippendales? (8)

blocks.note: the people chairing a company's annual general meeting, its most senior figures
read as the male strip troupe, but meant as the followers of Thomas Chippendale, the 18th-century furniture maker who made chairs

annotation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that the Chippendales strip troupe are the star turns at company meetings.
annotation.walkthrough: The Chippendales are male strippers, but Chippendale was also an 18th-century furniture maker, so they are chair men. An AGM is a company's annual general meeting.
annotation.definitionFit: Those who chair meetings are chairmen, and Chippendale's craftsmen made chairs, so the second sense is a punning one flagged by the question mark.

entries.clue: Man perhaps in offer to host Games (5)

indicatorNotes.to host: BID hosts PE, holding it inside

annotation.surface: A city bidding to host the Games.
annotation.walkthrough: The bid to host the Games reads like an Olympic bid; Games is school PE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': humans walk on two feet, so man is one kind of two-legged animal.

entries.clue: State benefits: who can say what the future holds? (8)

annotation.definition: who can say what the future holds?

indicatorNotes.State: to state is to say out loud

annotation.surface: A political question about welfare payments and whether anyone can predict them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State benefits' reads as welfare; 'State' is split off as the say-it instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Seers who foretell events are the people who can say what lies ahead, and the question mark marks the definition as a description.

entries.clue: Waterproofing marine network will take time (7)

annotation.surface: Weatherproofing an undersea cable network will be a slow job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marine network' looks like one thing; it breaks into SEA and LAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: the paste or coating used for waterproofing a joint is what this names.
annotation.definitionNote: Waterproofing is used as a noun, the material.

entries.clue: Sinatra cryptically leading line of stars! (6)

indicatorNotes.cryptically: read SINATRA as a cryptic instruction: S IN ATRA

blocks.note: S IN ATRA: put S inside ATRA to get A(S)TRA

annotation.surface: Frank Sinatra heading a line-up of stars.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the name as S-IN-ATRA and obey it: S goes inside ATRA. 'Stars' suggests celebrities like Sinatra, but it means heavenly bodies.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: from Latin astrum, star, as in astral bodies and astral projection.

entries.clue: Kicking GTI, one's in a rage (6)

indicatorNotes.in a rage: the letters are thrown about wildly

annotation.surface: An angry motorist kicking his GTI hatchback.
annotation.walkthrough: A GTI is a sporty car model; here its letters are simply fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Toeing a ball is striking it with the tip of the boot, a particular way of kicking.

entries.clue: Worried by debts one's taken on in advance (7)

indicatorNotes.taken on in advance: AN is attached at the front

blocks.note: x = by, as in 3 x 4 metres
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

annotation.surface: Someone fretting over debts taken on before being paid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worried by debts' reads as one idea; 'by' is its own piece, the multiplication sign in dimensions.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone fretting over debts is uneasy, nervous, worried.

entries.clue: Lucifer's rival (5)

blocks.note: read as the Devil, but meant as the Victorian name for a strike-anywhere light for fires and pipes
an equal or opponent, someone able to compete on level terms

annotation.surface: Who could be a match for the Devil?
annotation.walkthrough: Lucifer is the Devil, but a lucifer was also an old name for a friction match.
annotation.definitionFit: A lucifer was a Victorian friction match, and a match is also an equal who can compete with you; the two senses share the word.

entries.clue: Married woman captures the heart of karaoke bar (4)

indicatorNotes.captures: captures as in takes prisoner: MRS holds A inside it
indicatorNotes.the heart of: the heart is the centre, so take karaoke's middle letter

blocks.note: Mrs is a married woman's title

annotation.surface: A wife stealing the show at a karaoke bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Karaoke bar' reads as a venue; 'bar' is split off, and a Mars bar is a British chocolate bar.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by brand: a Mars is the best-known British chocolate bar, so 'bar' names it by its shape.
annotation.definitionNote: The definition names the thing; the answer is its brand name.

entries.clue: Carpets are being ruined by parties (9)

indicatorNotes.being ruined: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so ARE loses its order

annotation.surface: Rugs spoilt by guests at parties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carpets' is the verb, to reprimand, not floor coverings.
annotation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to scold them, and to earbash is to harangue at length.

entries.clue: Angel wanting massage? It's beyond a desire (4)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting in its sense of lacking: the angel is missing the massage
indicatorNotes.beyond: beyond means further along, so the remains come after A

blocks.note: a cherub is an angel; remove RUB
a rub is a massage, taken away from CHERUB to leave CHE

annotation.surface: An angel longing for a massage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting massage' reads as longing for one; 'wanting' means lacking, and 'It' is the leftover CHE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to long for something is to have a nagging want of it, the sense of 'desire'.
annotation.definitionNote: Desire is read as a verb, to long for.

entries.clue: Special key needed for compound (4)

blocks.note: the Alt key on a keyboard

annotation.surface: A particular key needed to get into a walled compound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compound' suggests an enclosure; it is the chemical sense, and salts are compounds.
annotation.definitionFit: A salt is a chemical compound, such as sodium chloride.

entries.clue: Back boiler put in new position (9)

blocks.note: a range is a kitchen stove that can also heat water

annotation.surface: A plumber moving the back boiler somewhere else.
annotation.walkthrough: A back boiler sits behind a fire to heat water; split it and 'boiler' is a range cooker.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: moving furniture into a new position is to reorder it.

entries.clue: Fashionable English learner driver's one after Golf? (5)

blocks.note: the L-plate on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A trendy English learner driver hoping to take up golf.
annotation.walkthrough: In the NATO alphabet Hotel follows Golf; the question mark flags that this is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: In the phonetic alphabet, Hotel is the word after Golf.
